clue.text: It makes me boil inside when one is used at the pub

definitions.text: It makes me boil inside when one is used at the pub

parts.words: It makes me boil inside when one is used at the pub
parts.note: a cryptic description of the gadget whose ringing and chatter in a quiet bar infuriates other drinkers; slyly, the letters of ME BOIL also rearrange into the first word

explanation.surface: A grumpy drinker fumes about something other people do in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a complaint about a pub nuisance; it describes the device itself, and 'me boil' happens to be an anagram of its first word as a bonus hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the portable handset whose use in pubs annoys fellow customers.

clue.text: Writer above the common herd uses weightlifting and treadmill

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first pieces sit above the last one

parts.note: split as weight lifting: a gram is a weight, and lifting it in a down entry reads it upwards
split as tread mill: the letters of tread are milled, ground into a new order
the rabble is the common herd, the mob

explanation.surface: A novelist who thinks herself superior to ordinary people keeps fit at the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: Weightlifting and the treadmill paint a gym, but each word splits in two: the gram is lifted, and the tread is milled. Margaret Drabble is an English novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Drabble is a celebrated English novelist and editor of literary reference works.

clue.text: Initiate Israeli leader

definitions.meaning: to initiate is to start something off
Menachem ... was Prime Minister of Israel from 1977 to 1983

explanation.definitionFit: To initiate means to start; Menachem Begin was a prime minister of Israel.

clue.text: Girl allowed it to turn fine

parts.note: to let is to allow
taken as written

indicators.note: the letters for fine are turned around, read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, fine; the 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A girl was permitted to let something become fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' reverses AI (A1, with the figure one read as I) to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Letitia is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Compiler has no right to become controversial

indicators.note: the remaining letters are made into something new, rearranged

parts.note: the fodder word as written

explanation.surface: A crossword setter, losing the right, turns argumentative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' removes R from COMPILER, and 'to become' rearranges the remaining COMPILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Polemic as an adjective means controversial or disputatious, though it is usually a noun for a fierce attack.

clue.text: Love letter not revealing all

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
a missive is a letter

explanation.surface: A love letter that keeps some secrets back.
explanation.definitionFit: Omissive means characterised by omission, leaving things out.

clue.text: MOT said to get one started better

definitions.text: MOT said to get one started better

parts.words: MOT said to get one started better
parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for cars; here the M.O.T. is something taken just after waking to get a person going for the day

explanation.surface: A car's annual test is claimed to help the engine start more readily.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly roadworthiness test for vehicles, which makes 'started' look like an engine; it is a person being got going by a cuppa.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuppa brought first thing on waking is a traditional way to get going for the day.

clue.text: Checked the dog basket?

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
a dog's basket is its bed

explanation.surface: Was the dog's basket inspected?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads as a cur's bed, a dog basket.
explanation.definitionFit: Curbed means restrained or held in check.

clue.text: Pals come round in French town

indicators.note: the friends surround the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: amis is French for friends or pals
en is French for in

explanation.surface: Friends gather in a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' looks like part of the definition, but it goes with 'in' to give EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiens is a cathedral city in northern France.

clue.text: Success to the Tories for being honest!

parts.note: the cheer 'Up the ...!' wishes success to a side
the Tories are the political right

explanation.surface: A cheer for the Conservatives on account of their integrity.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright person is honest and of good moral character.

clue.text: Lie about 19 in Ireland

indicators.note: the letters of lie are moved about, rearranged

parts.note: the fodder word as written
the answer to 19 across means cut, here a synonym, trim

explanation.surface: A fib about a cross-reference set in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LIE to LEI; 19 across means cut, so TRIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Leitrim is a county in the north-west of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Stoker keeps in step, almost a necessity for bodily function

indicators.note: the author's name holds the following letters inside it

parts.note: Bram Stoker wrote Dracula
taken as written

indicators.note: the last letter of step is dropped

explanation.surface: A stoker keeps pace with something nearly essential to the body.
explanation.walkthrough: Bram Stoker, the author of Dracula, supplies the outer letters; the step is shortened, and the whole thing is split after BRA.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of the brain joined to the spinal cord controls breathing and heartbeat, so the body cannot function without it.

clue.text: Manner of one up the pole who's lost it?

indicators.note: the pole-sitter has lost a piece, which is removed

parts.note: a stylite was an ascetic saint who lived on top of a pillar
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about the bearing of someone up a pole who has lost his nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: A stylite, like St Simeon, lived atop a pillar; removing IT from STYLITE leaves the answer. 'Lost it' looks like losing one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Style is a manner or way of doing something.

clue.text: You can snuff it prematurely if this is poor

definitions.text: You can snuff it prematurely if this is poor

parts.words: You can snuff it prematurely if this is poor
parts.note: a bad eating regime can lead to early death; to snuff it is slang for to die, which also opens the answer

explanation.surface: A warning that bad food can kill you young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snuff it' is slang for die, which happens to give the first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: What a person habitually eats, which if unhealthy shortens life.

clue.text: So USA civil administration is wanton?

indicators.note: the letters are administered, managed into a new order

parts.note: fodder as written
fodder as written
fodder as written

explanation.surface: Is American civil government therefore lewd?
explanation.walkthrough: 'administration' looks like the US government, but it signals rearranging SOUSACIVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lascivious means lustful or lewd, as wanton does in its sexual sense.

clue.text: Overbearing bitch with no tail to credit

parts.note: a bitch is a female dog, playfully a dog mother, or 'dog ma'

indicators.note: the word for credit loses its last letter

parts.note: to buy on tick is to buy on credit

explanation.surface: A domineering woman refuses to give anyone credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitch' is read as a dog's ma, DOG + MA; 'with no tail' cuts TICK to TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogmatic person asserts opinions in an arrogant, overbearing way.

clue.text: Hamilton I'd wrongly placed farther east

indicators.note: the letters are put in the wrong positions, rearranged

parts.note: fodder as written
fodder as written

explanation.surface: Someone has mislocated the Scottish town of Hamilton too far east.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamilton is a town in Lanarkshire, west of Edinburgh; the answer is a Scottish council area lying to its east.
explanation.definitionFit: Midlothian, around Edinburgh, lies further east in Scotland than Hamilton does.

clue.text: Prison needs space for erection in deserts

indicators.note: in a down clue, erecting the pieces turns them upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: stir is slang for prison
an em is a printer's space

explanation.surface: A jail needs room to put up a building in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for erection' turns STIREM upwards. 'deserts' here is what one deserves, as in just deserts.
explanation.definitionFit: One's deserts are what one deserves, one's due rewards or punishments.

clue.text: Sufficient land for the race training?

indicators.note: the letters are trained into a new arrangement

parts.note: fodder as written
fodder as written

explanation.surface: Is there enough ground to train racehorses?
explanation.walkthrough: 'training' rearranges THE RACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hectare is a metric area of land of 10,000 square metres.

clue.text: Mother of twins taken up by classic character in the theatre

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking a word up reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: Leda bore the twins Castor and Pollux in Greek myth
phi is a letter of the classical Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A mother of twins is adopted by a famous classical figure at the playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' reverses LEDA to ADEL. The Adelphi is a theatre in London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adelphi is a West End theatre on the Strand in London.

clue.text: Supports about to be cut

indicators.note: the word for supports is turned about, read backwards

parts.note: pins are legs, which support the body

explanation.surface: Supporting beams are about to be cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'about to', but it reverses PINS.
explanation.definitionFit: To snip is to cut with small quick strokes of scissors.

clue.text: Nationality could be French

definitions.meaning: the nationality of people from Poland
French ... is a glossy shellac finish for furniture

explanation.surface: A nationality that might turn out to be French.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish is the nationality of Poland, and French polish is a wood finish.

clue.text: Domain partial to a football team?

indicators.note: only part of the club's name is used, its last letters dropped

parts.note: Real Madrid is a famous Spanish football club

explanation.surface: A territory whose people support a certain football side?
explanation.walkthrough: 'partial to' looks like being fond of a team; it means taking only part of REAL MADRID.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain or kingdom.

clue.text: It's characteristic of the Trinity to display tolerance

indicators.note: the letters are put on display in a new arrangement

parts.note: fodder as written

explanation.surface: Showing forbearance is typical of the Holy Trinity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to display' rearranges TOLERANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The three persons of the Trinity are held to be equally eternal, existing together without beginning.

clue.text: Broken heart standing by an open grave

indicators.note: the word heart is broken up and rearranged

parts.note: fodder as written

explanation.surface: A grieving mourner stands heartbroken at a graveside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges HEART.
explanation.definitionFit: The soil dug out of a grave is piled beside it until the burial.

clue.text: Habitat ruined her

indicators.note: the word habitat is wrecked and its letters rearranged

parts.note: fodder as written

explanation.surface: A woman's environment has been destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges HABITAT; 'her' stands for a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabitha is a woman's given name, so 'her' stands for it.

clue.text: Mineral used in sung holy ceremonies

indicators.note: what is sung is heard, so the sound of the words counts

parts.note: pi is crossword slang for pious or holy, and rites are ceremonies

explanation.surface: A mineral used in chanted religious services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sung' signals the sound: PI RITES is said the same as the mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyrites is a sulphide mineral, iron pyrites being fool's gold.

clue.text: Dutch artist, 99, almost hit by a type of bacteria

parts.note: M. C. Escher was a Dutch graphic artist
IC is 99 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the word for hit loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A Dutch artist aged 99 is nearly struck by a germ.
explanation.walkthrough: IC as 99 is a loose Roman numeral (strictly XCIX); 'almost' cuts HIT to HI.
explanation.definitionFit: Escherichia is the bacterial genus that includes E. coli.
